# S55 — Run tree: orchestrator, roles and steps with live status

Owner 2026-10-20 (#110, ui.run-tree): see what step is running, under the orchestrator, as a tree. The tree shows in the S26 detail pane: the orchestrator, then its roles and steps with a state glyph (running, done, failed, waiting) and a spinner on each running step, with role, vendor, model, phase and elapsed time. Data: for an engine run the roles in the run record; for a ledger run the steps with their parent (slicer relay-run list shows the nesting; relay-run step --parent). The animated flow diagram, stage bars and charts stay in S07, which builds on this tree. S30 shows the running role on a row; this slice shows the whole tree.

## Why

A row says a run is active with N steps running but not which. The owner wants to see the tree of who is doing what.

## Files

- `internal/source` and `internal/slicercli`: the step fields the tree needs (id, parent, role, agent, vendor, model, reasoning, phase, task, times) come from the ledger JSON. source.Snapshot.Runs (`internal/source/source.go:73`) already holds the full steps of active runs; check the field names with slicer relay-run list --json before building.
- `internal/daemon`: carry the engine run's roles on the EngineRun wire (built at `internal/daemon/runs.go:716`). Owner 2026-10-22: no `tree` field on daemon.Relay (`internal/daemon/wire.go:99`); ork status keeps counts only.
- `internal/tui`: the tree in the S26 pane, spinner on running steps (a tick; no goroutine in Update), Enter on a started-elsewhere row opens a read-only pane, tests, goldens.
- `docs/dashboard.md` (dash.role-detail), `docs/state.md` or design.md where they list the wire.

## Failing tests

- A ledger run with steps and parents renders as a tree: the orchestrator at the root, its steps beneath, children indented under their parent step.
- Each node shows a state glyph, role, model and phase; a running node shows a spinner frame that advances on a tick; a failed node is marked.
- An engine run shows its roles (implementer, reviewer, gate) as a tree under the run with the same glyphs.
- A step whose parent is unknown or missing is shown at the root, not dropped.
- A long task text is cut to fit the width; 80-column and narrow layouts keep the tree readable.
- Monochrome and colour golden views; the spinner has an ASCII fallback.
- Runs started elsewhere: Enter on the row opens the pane with the tree, read-only (no action keys). This replaces the "ledger" case of the existing test at `internal/tui/pane_test.go:136-141`, which asserted no pane.

## Implement

Verified ledger fields: `slicer relay-run list --json --lean` gives runs[] with id, items, worktree, begun_at, updated_at, state, outcome, counts and steps. Each step has id, role, agent, vendor, model, reasoning, phase, task, parent, begun_at and updated_at. internal/slicercli/types.go:132 (Step) and :156 (RelayRun) already parse them. --lean drops empty fields, so a missing parent means root. Phases in the current output: done and fail. ork writes "start" (stepStart, internal/engine/round.go:355), but no sampled run had a running step.
1. Write the failing tests first in internal/tui/runtree_test.go (new). Reuse testdata/cli/slicer/relay-run-list.json and add a tree sample.
2. internal/slicercli/types.go: Step and RelayRun need no change.
3. The TUI reads snapshots from source directly (internal/tui/model.go:238), and source.Snapshot.Runs (internal/source/source.go:73, fetched at :105 and :138 with active only) already holds each run's steps. No source or daemon.Relay change for ledger runs (owner 2026-10-22: no `tree` wire field).
4. Engine runs with RelayRun set already have each role round as a ledger step under the orchestrator step (round.go:355). Show the ledger tree in that case. Without RelayRun, build the tree from runrec.Record.Roles (internal/runrec/record.go:46-62); RoleRecord.Step links to the ledger step. Never show both.
5. Add the engine run's roles to EngineRun (internal/source/source.go:159, built at internal/daemon/runs.go:716). Proposed fields.
6. internal/tui/pane.go: paneRow (pane.go:23-32) finds engine runs only. Let it also find a started-elsewhere ledger row, with no action keys and no answer input. Add runTreeLines(steps, width, frame) (new function), used in paneLines (pane.go:88).
7. Build the tree from parent ids. Children go under their parent. A missing parent goes to the root. Keep a visited set so a loop cannot hang.
8. Glyphs: phase "start" is running (spinner frame), "done" and "fail" as named. Any other phase shows its raw text with a neutral glyph. Owner 2026-10-22: no "waiting" glyph; no ledger phase means waiting.
9. Spinner: a frame index advanced by a tick message. Reuse tickMsg (internal/tui/model.go:48, handled at :247). No goroutine in Update. Mono frames are ASCII: | / - \.
10. Clip the task text with the existing clip helper (internal/tui/overview.go:386), so 80-column and narrow layouts stay readable.
11. docs/dashboard.md:257-266 (dash.role-detail): describe the tree.
12. Goldens: go test ./internal/tui -update, then review the diff in testdata/golden/ (colour and mono, 80x24 and 100x30).
Notes:
- An engine run without RelayRun has RoleRecords with no parent, so its roles render flat under the run. This matches the item text.
